name: What materials are used to replace polybutylene pipes?

mainEntity.name: What materials are used to replace polybutylene pipes?

acceptedAnswer.text: When replacing polybutylene pipes, the most common and recommended materials are PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) and copper. PEX is flexible, corrosion-resistant, and less expensive to install, often requiring fewer connections. Copper is durable, long-lasting, and recyclable, known for its proven reliability. Both are superior alternatives to polybutylene, each with distinct advantages. Alpha-Plumbing Services can discuss the pros and cons of each option to help you choose the best fit for your home and budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common replacements are PEX (flexible, corrosion-resistant, cost-effective) and copper (durable, long-lasting). Both are superior to polybutylene.
